meaning: No milk. A Kopi O is black coffee with sugar; add Kosong for no sugar too.
origin: From the Hokkien word for black.

meaning: Evaporated milk instead of condensed milk, with sugar added separately. Creamier and less sweet than a plain Kopi.
origin: Often said to come from the Hainanese word for fresh, or from the Carnation brand of evaporated milk. People still argue about it.

meaning: No sugar. Condensed milk is already sweet, so a drink made with it can’t be Kosong; said on its own, “Kopi Kosong” is taken to mean Kopi O Kosong.
Less sweet: about half the usual sugar or condensed milk.
origin: From the Hokkien for less sweet.

meaning: Sweeter: more sugar or condensed milk than usual.
origin: From the Hokkien for add sweet.

meaning: Stronger: more coffee, tea or Milo in the same cup.
Weaker: less coffee or tea and more water. A good way to have less caffeine.
Undiluted: no water is added after brewing or mixing, so the drink is as strong and rich as it gets.
origin: From the Hokkien, roughly “straight from the source”.

meaning: Iced. Kopi Peng, Teh Peng and Milo Peng all come over ice.
origin: From the Hokkien word for ice.

meaning: Takeaway. Add it to the end of your order when you want to take the drink with you; it often comes in a plastic bag with a string handle.
origin: From the Cantonese for pack it up.

meaning: Another name for Milo, still heard at older kopitiams.
origin: From the Hokkien for kick ball, after the football players on old Milo tins and adverts.

meaning: Thick, sweetened milk. A plain Kopi or Teh is made with it unless you ask for O or C.
origin: Tinned condensed milk kept well without a fridge, so early kopitiams used it from the start.

meaning: Unsweetened milk cooked down until creamy. It is the C in Kopi C and Teh C.
origin: Like condensed milk, it came in tins and kept well in the heat.

meaning: The coffee used at kopitiams: mostly robusta, roasted dark with a little sugar and margarine, and ground fine.
origin: The roast began as a way to make cheaper beans taste rich. Many families still buy it from the same roaster for years.
